summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (LVEF 20%), ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was admitted for acute worsening of shortness of breath and chest discomfort following a missed dose of torsemide due to medication noncompliance during a period of housing instability. He presented with volume overload, weight gain, bibasilar crackles, and elevated BNP of 4403, consistent with acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation. Treatment included aggressive IV diuresis with Lasix and metolazone, leading to improved symptoms and a discharge weight of 128.7 kg. His creatinine rose to 2.5 due to diuresis, prompting a temporary reduction in torsemide to every other day with plans to reassess based on renal function. He was started on spironolactone and continued on his baseline heart failure and diabetes medications. Psychiatry evaluated him for adjustment-related hopelessness but found no clinical depression. He declined right heart catheterization for volume assessment. He was discharged to an extended care facility for rehabilitation with close outpatient follow-up for medication titration, lab monitoring, and support for adherence and emotional well-being.
